extracted.intended_audience: applicants/sponsors of new drug and abbreviated applications, drug manufacturers/distributors, DMF holders, and regulatory/legal counsel interacting with FDA
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory requirements and procedural standards under 21 CFR Part 314 covering documentation, hearings, public disclosure, drug master files, imports/exports, accelerated approval, and animal-efficacy approvals for new drug products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of formulation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement whether such formulation has at any subsequent time been changed in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any such change has been made, the exact date, nature, and rationale for each change in formulation, including any deletion or change in the concentration of any active ingredient and/or inactive ingredient, should be stated, together with a copy of each pertinent document or record to establish the date and nature of each such change, including, but not limited to, the formula which resulted from each such change. If no such change has been made, a copy of representative documents or records showing the formula at representative points in time should be submitted to support the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling documentation and change history
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a copy of each pertinent document or record establishing identity of each item of written, printed, or graphic matter used as labeling on the date the drug was initially marketed, and state whether labeling has been discontinued or changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If labeling was discontinued or changed, submit the exact date, nature, and rationale for each discontinuance or change and copies of pertinent documents, including the resulting labeling. If no change occurred, supply representative documents showing labeling at representative points in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing date documentation and discontinuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documents establishing the exact date the drug was initially marketed and state whether marketing has at any subsequent time been discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If marketing was discontinued, submit the exact date(s) and copies of each pertinent document or record to establish each such date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification statement and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement signed by the person responsible that all appropriate records have been searched and that, to the best of that person's knowledge and belief, the submission includes a true and accurate presentation of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: A willfully false statement is a criminal offense (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: No FDA exemption for products described in §310.6
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not find a drug product (including active ingredients) identical, related, or similar as described in §310.6 to be exempt from part or all of the new drug provisions if an application is or has been effective, deemed approved, or approved under section 505.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to support contention that product is not a new drug
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contention that a drug product is not a new drug for any other reason must be supported by submission of the factual records, data, and information necessary and appropriate to support the contention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to maintain 'grandfather' documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons manufacturing or distributing a drug in reliance upon a 'grandfather' provision must maintain files that fully document and support that status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions upon request for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation of functions commences upon receipt of a request for hearing: CDER prepares analysis and proposed order which, with the request and proposed denials, will be submitted to the Office of the Commissioner for review and decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When CDER recommends denial of a hearing on all issues, no representative of the Center will participate in the Commissioner's review/decision. If CDER recommends granting hearing on one or more issues, separation terminates as to those issues; Commissioner may modify issue text but may not deny a hearing on those issues. Failure to move to include denied issues constitutes waiver. Office of General Counsel observes same separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific facts requirement to avoid summary judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A person requesting a hearing may not rely on allegations or denials but must set forth specific facts showing a genuine and substantial issue of fact requiring a hearing for the particular drug product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for summary judgment against hearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner will enter summary judgment and deny a hearing if it conclusively appears from the face of the data, information, and factual analyses in the request that there is no genuine and substantial issue of fact precluding refusal to approve or withdrawal of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any order entering summary judgment must set forth the Commissioner's findings and conclusions in detail and specify why each study submitted fails to meet statutory/regulatory requirements (e.g., lack of adequate and well-controlled clinical investigations meeting §314.126 and, for combination products, §300.50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed order denying hearing and 60-day response
rubrics_metrics.description: When Director of CDER concludes summary judgment should be considered, Director will serve a proposed order denying a hearing by registered mail, and the person has 60 days after receipt to respond with sufficient data, information, and analyses to demonstrate a genuine and substantial issue of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies following general notice of opportunity for a hearing or when submissions are of a type required by statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's entry of summary judgment for requester
rubrics_metrics.description: If review shows the grounds cited in the notice are not valid (e.g., substantial evidence of effectiveness exists), the Commissioner will enter summary judgment for the person requesting the hearing and rescind the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for commencement of hearing if granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner grants a hearing, it will begin within 90 days after the expiration of the time for requesting the hearing unless otherwise agreed (denial of approval) and as soon as practicable in withdrawal cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for granting a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will grant a hearing if a genuine and substantial issue of fact exists or if the Commissioner concludes that a hearing would be in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing scope for identical/related product manufacturer
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manufacturer/distributor of an identical, related, or similar drug product requests and is granted a hearing, the hearing may consider whether the product is identical, related, or similar to the drug named in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a hearing, and any subsequent grant or denial, applies only to the drug products named in such documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal notice and declaration of unlawfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will issue a notice withdrawing approval and declaring products unlawful for drug products subject to a notice of opportunity for a hearing for which an opportunity is waived or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may defer or stay the action pending related requests or proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importation criteria for new drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: A new drug may be imported if it is the subject of an approved application under this part or it complies with the investigational new drug regulations under part 312 and general import regulations under subpart E of part 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A drug substance intended for manufacture/processing/repacking may be imported if it complies with the labeling exemption in §201.122 pertaining to shipments of drug substances in domestic commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export criteria for new drugs and drug substances
rubrics_metrics.description: A new drug may be exported if subject of an approved application or it complies with IND regulations under part 312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A drug substance covered by an approved application for use in manufacture of an approved product may be exported by the applicant or listed suppliers provided it meets approved product specifications and is shipped with a copy of the required labeling. Insulin or an antibiotic may be exported without regard to section 802 if it meets section 801(e)(1) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of a Drug Master File (DMF)
rubrics_metrics.description: A DMF is a submission of information to FDA by a person (DMF holder) intended to be used to permit incorporation by reference when submitting INDs, applications, abbreviated applications, amendments, or to authorize others to rely on the information without disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA ordinarily neither independently reviews nor approves DMFs but reviews them in context of an application. A DMF may contain information required for any submission, including drug substance, intermediates, packaging, excipients, or FDA-accepted reference information. For DMF content not covered by Types II-IV, a letter of intent must be submitted first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of DMF content
rubrics_metrics.description: An IND, application, abbreviated application, amendment, or supplement may incorporate by reference all or part of the contents of any DMF if the holder authorizes the incorporation in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each incorporation must describe the incorporated material by name, reference number, volume, and page number of the DMF.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMF copies and notification of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A DMF must be submitted in two copies. If the DMF holder adds, changes, or deletes information (except the list required under paragraph (d)), the holder shall notify in writing each person authorized to reference that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any addition/change/deletion (except the list) must be submitted in two copies and describe by name, reference number, volume, and page number the information affected in the DMF.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMF list of authorized persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMF must contain a complete list of each person currently authorized to incorporate by reference any information in the file, identifying by name, reference number, volume, and page number the information each person is authorized to incorporate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorization is restricted to particular drug products, include the name of each drug product and application number, if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of application and DMF information (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will determine public availability of any part of an application or abbreviated application under this section and part 20; application includes all data submitted with or incorporated by reference including INDs, DMFs, supplements, reports, and other submissions. Safety and effectiveness data include all animal and human studies and tests for identity, stability, purity, potency, and bioavailability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-disclosure of existence of application before approval letter
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not publicly disclose the existence of an application or abbreviated application before an approval letter is sent, unless the existence has been previously publicly disclosed or acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If existence not publicly disclosed or acknowledged, no data or information in the application is available for public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited discretionary disclosure before approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If existence has been publicly disclosed before approval, no data are available for public disclosure before approval, but the Commissioner may, in his/her discretion, disclose a summary of selected portions of safety and effectiveness data appropriate for public consideration of a specific pending issue (e.g., open advisory committee session).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of particular materials after approval
rubrics_metrics.description: After FDA sends an approval letter, specified data and information become immediately available for public disclosure unless applicant shows extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: summaries of safety/effectiveness data (Summaries or Summary Basis of Approval (SBA)), protocols (unless trade secret), adverse reaction reports and consumer complaints (with identifying information deleted), lists of active/inactive ingredients previously disclosed, certain assay procedures (unless trade secret or no regulatory purpose), and correspondence or summaries of oral discussions between FDA and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for SBAs and pre-/post-1975 differences
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications approved before July 1, 1975, internal agency records describing safety/effectiveness are disclosed after deletion of identifying information and inappropriate gratuitous comments. For applications approved on/after July 1, 1975, a Summary Basis of Approval (SBA) will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SBA may be prepared as a draft by the applicant (which CDER will review) or by CDER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions making all safety/effectiveness data available
rubrics_metrics.description: All safety/effectiveness data and information submitted in an application and not previously disclosed are available to the public upon request at the time any one of enumerated events occurs (e.g., no work to approve, final determination application not approvable and appeals exhausted, approval withdrawn and appeals exhausted, final determination drug is not a new drug, for 505(b) the effective date of first ANDA referencing the drug, for 505(j) when FDA sends approval letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information not available for public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless previously disclosed or relating to an abandoned product and not a trade secret/confidential commercial info, the following are not available for public disclosure: manufacturing methods or processes (including quality control procedures); production, sales distribution and similar data (except aggregated compilations that do not reveal nondisclosable info); quantitative or semiquantitative formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of compilations and §20.117 materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Compilations of information specified in §20.117 are available for public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and correspondence delivery addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall send applications, abbreviated applications, and other correspondence related to this part to the offices and addresses specified (Central Document Room; Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research for listed products; field copy to home FDA district office; foreign applicants to specified addresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific routing: submissions under §§314.50/314.54 to Central Document Room (with exceptions); abbreviated applications under §314.94 similarly; requests for opportunity for hearing under §314.110 directed to Associate Director for Policy (HFD-5); field copy rules apply; special product lists for CBER have specified address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA has made available guidance documents under §10.115 to help comply with certain requirements of this part; CDER maintains a list of guidance documents that apply to CDER regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is maintained on the Internet and published annually in the Federal Register. Requests for a copy of the CDER list directed to the Office of Training and Communications, Division of Drug Information, CDER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated approval scope (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart applies to certain new drug products studied for safety and effectiveness in treating serious or life‑threatening illnesses and that provide meaningful therapeutic benefit to patients over existing treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ability to treat patients unresponsive to available therapy, or improved patient response over available therapy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval based on surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant marketing approval on the basis of adequate and well‑controlled clinical trials establishing an effect on a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, or an effect on a clinical endpoint other than survival or irreversible morbidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval under this section will be subject to requirement that the applicant study the drug further to verify and describe clinical benefit when there is uncertainty about the relation of the surrogate to clinical benefit or observed clinical benefit to ultimate outcome. Postmarketing studies would usually be already underway; when required they must be adequate and well‑controlled and conducted with due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval with restrictions to assure safe use
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA concludes a drug shown effective can be safely used only if distribution/use is restricted, FDA will require postmarketing restrictions as needed to assure safe use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: distribution restricted to certain facilities or physicians with special training/experience; distribution conditioned on performance of specified medical procedures. Limitations imposed will be commensurate with the specific safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal procedures for accelerated approvals (grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: For drugs approved under §§314.510 and 314.520, FDA may withdraw approval (following part 15 hearing as modified) if any of enumerated grounds occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include: (1) postmarketing clinical study fails to verify clinical benefit; (2) applicant fails to perform required postmarketing study with due diligence; (3) use after marketing demonstrates restrictions inadequate; (4) applicant fails to adhere to agreed postmarketing restrictions; (5) promotional materials are false or misleading; (6) other evidence demonstrates the drug is not shown to be safe or effective under its conditions of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opportunity for hearing and required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Director of CDER will give applicant notice of an opportunity for a hearing on proposed withdrawal, ordinarily a letter stating general reasons and proposed grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to file a written request for a hearing within 15 days of receipt, applicant waives the opportunity. If a timely request is filed, the agency will publish notice of hearing in the Federal Register. An applicant who requests a hearing must, within 30 days of receipt of the notice of opportunity for a hearing, submit the data and information upon which the applicant intends to rely at the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions waiver in withdrawal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation of functions (as specified in §10.55) will not apply at any point in withdrawal proceedings under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified hearing procedures for withdrawal under accelerated approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings will be conducted under part 15 with modifications: an advisory committee will be present to review issues and provide advice; presiding officer, advisory committee members, up to three applicant representatives, and up to three Center representatives may question any person during or at the conclusion of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other person attending may question a presenter; presiding officer may permit questions submitted for response by a presenter as a matter of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and stay petition prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner's decision constitutes final agency action from which the applicant may petition for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before requesting a court stay pending review, applicant must first submit a petition for a stay of action under §10.35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing safety reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Drug products approved under this accelerated program are subject to postmarketing recordkeeping and safety reporting applicable to all approved drug products as provided in §§314.80 and 314.81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing for promotional materials for products under review
rubrics_metrics.description: For drugs considered for approval under this subpart, applicants must submit to the agency during the preapproval review period copies of all promotional materials intended for dissemination or publication within 120 days following marketing approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After 120 days following marketing approval, unless otherwise informed, the applicant must submit promotional materials at least 30 days prior to the intended initial dissemination of the labeling or initial publication of the advertisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of accelerated-approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA determines after approval that requirements established in §§314.520, 314.530, or 314.550 are no longer necessary for safe and effective use, it will notify the applicant and terminate those requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily, for §314.510 approvals, requirements will no longer apply when the required postmarketing study verifies and describes clinical benefit and product would be appropriate for traditional approval. For §314.520 approvals, restrictions end when safe use can be assured through labeling. FDA may also remove specific postapproval requirements upon petition review under §10.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope for approval when human efficacy studies are unethical/unfeasible (Subpart I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to new drug products studied for safety/efficacy in preventing serious or life‑threatening conditions caused by lethal/permanently disabling toxic biological, chemical, radiological, or nuclear substances when definitive human efficacy studies cannot be conducted and field trials are not feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply to products approvable by other FDA efficacy standards (e.g., accelerated approval) and does not address safety evaluation for these products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for approval based on adequate and well-controlled animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant marketing approval based on adequate and well‑controlled animal studies when results establish the drug is reasonably likely to produce clinical benefit in humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will rely on animal evidence only when: (1) there is a reasonably well‑understood pathophysiological mechanism of toxicity and its prevention/substantial reduction by the product; (2) effect is demonstrated in more than one animal species expected to react predictively for humans (unless single species is sufficiently well‑characterized); (3) animal study endpoint is clearly related to desired human benefit (generally enhancement of survival or prevention of major morbidity); and (4) kinetics/pharmacodynamics data in animals and humans allow selection of an effective human dose. Agency may also consider other data, including human data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing study requirement for animal‑efficacy approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval under this subpart will be subject to requirements that the applicant conduct postmarketing studies (e.g., field studies) to verify and describe clinical benefit and to assess safety when such studies are feasible and ethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such studies would not be feasible until an exigency arises. When feasible, the applicant must conduct such studies with due diligence.
